text.p: Italian debt markets took a step back by late trade after a choppy day in which dealers said the Btp lacked the strength to push on higher for now.
"It's been up and down like a yo-yo, it's been a very stressful day," one broker in London said.

Traders said the Btp market had gained strongly recently. "The Italian market didn't have the strength to go further. We had a double top on the 60 minute (Sept LIFFE) chart at 138.35 and that was the signal that that was it for today," the London broker said. The Sept LIFFE contract was 14 basis points down at 137.90 by late trade.
The February 2007 cash Btp closed 16 basis points down at 103.46 and the yield was 6.35 percent with a spread over the 10-year Bund of 83 basis points.
The lira inched back from a stronger position against the mark, standing at 974.00/4.50 per mark in late European trade compared with 972.00 late on Wednesday.

Dealers said there was no news driving the market, after the Bundesbank left its repo rate steady at three percent for the next two weeks, although they said investors were starting to think about the possibility of German rate movements later in the year. "At the moment it's all just speculation," one said.
